items.text: $F\colon C\to C'$ commuting with finite products and with the final object carries group objects of $C$ to group objects of $C'$:
F(X\times X)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }F(X)\times F(X),\qquad F(X)\times F(X)\xrightarrow{\ F(\pi)\circ(\,\cdot\,)^{-1}\ }F(X)
Associativity (diagram) is preserved if $F$ commutes with threefold products; the unit, if $F(\text{final})=\text{final}$; inverses likewise.

$F$ commuting with the finite inverse limits occurring in the axioms of a structure carries such structures in $C$ to structures of the same type in $C'$ (groups, rings, modules, objects with a group acting).
Fix a ring $k$. $C$ = category of affine algebraic spaces over $k$ = representable functors $C_k\to\mathbf{Sets}$ ($C_k$ the $k$-algebras):
Group structure on an affine space
A group structure on $X$: for every $Z$ a group structure on $X(Z)$, functorial in $Z$; with $Z=\operatorname{Spec}k'$,
Group law on $X$ = factorisation of $X\colon C_k\to\mathbf{Sets}$ through $\mathbf{Groups}$ (each $X(k')\to X(k'')$ a homomorphism).
An affine algebraic group over $k$ = a functor $C_k\to\mathbf{Groups}$ whose underlying functor to $\mathbf{Sets}$ is representable.
\mathrm{GL}_n(k')=\{n\times n\text{ invertible matrices over }k'\},\ \text{law: matrix product}
